editorial.marketOverview: Reuters reports an early Monday rebound of nearly 3% in Nasdaq-100 futures and 2% in S&P futures after Friday's semiconductor liquidation. Korean shares meanwhile declined more than 3%. The stronger futures bounce supports a possible Monday relief rally, not a verified US cash-session trend reversal.
editorial.whatChanged: Compared with the prior Sunday evening snapshot, the Reuters futures indication strengthened from about +2% to nearly +3% in Nasdaq-100 futures, with South Korean equities falling. This is incremental confirmation of the already-identified relief-bounce possibility; no material change to the three-day bearish outlook or curated Open Watch feed.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Overnight futures strength after a large selloff can reflect short covering. Friday SOX underperformance and weak breadth remain the principal downside evidence. No synchronized cash-session SOX, VXN/VIX, yields, oil or FedWatch observations confirm a durable turn; regional Asian reactions should not be confused with US cash-market behavior.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday November 23: higher chance of a relief-rally opening; flash PMIs at 09:45 ET and QQQ/SOX cash breadth decide durability. Tuesday November 24: consumer confidence and Dell earnings after close may renew AI spending concerns. Wednesday November 25: PCE/GDP at 08:30 ET and Beige Book at 14:00 ET may reset rate expectations. Bearish elevated downside risk remains the baseline with pronounced two-way volatility.
editorial.bullCase: Futures gains hold into QQQ and SOX/SMH cash strength, breadth turns positive and VXN/VIX decline while yields stabilize. A constructive PMI and inflation path supports a multi-session oversold rebound.
editorial.bearCase: Futures gains fade in US cash trading, chip stocks continue to lag, breadth remains weak and volatility or oil rises. Wednesday inflation or AI spending disappointments could restart liquidation.
editorial.watchNext: Confirm futures contract/timestamps; observe Monday QQQ, SOX/SMH, breadth, VXN/VIX, synchronized 2Y and 10Y percent yields and basis-point spread, CME FedWatch, contract-matched Brent/WTI, PMIs and new Open Watch events.
